title: Sources
text:
The data used in this project was sourced from the World Bank’s World Development Indicators (WDI) database, accessed through the WDI package in R.

📊 Selected Indicators
Three key economic indicators were retrieved for analysis:

GDP (current US$) – NY.GDP.MKTP.CD

Fiscal Balance (% of GDP) – GC.BAL.CASH.GD.ZS

Trade (% of GDP) – NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS

These indicators provide a foundational view of macroeconomic trends relevant to fiscal policy and trade openness.


🌏 Geographic Scope
The dataset focuses on SAARC member countries, specifically:

Afghanistan (AFG)

Bangladesh (BGD)

Bhutan (BTN)

India (IND)

Maldives (MDV)

Nepal (NPL)

Pakistan (PAK)

Sri Lanka (LKA)

Data was collected for the period 2000 to 2024, covering nearly 25 years of regional economic activity.


🧹 Data Cleaning and Preparation
The following data preparation steps were performed:

Renamed variables for clarity (gdp, fiscal, trade)
Filtered out rows with missing (NA) values in any of the three key indicators
Created a derived variable for GDP in billions (gdp_billion) to improve readability in plots

All processing was conducted in R using tidyverse conventions to ensure reproducibility and transparency.

title: About
text:
I’m Faran Abbas, a graduate student specializing in World Economy. My academic interests include international trade, fiscal policy, and economic development in emerging markets. You can explore my work and projects on GitHub, or reach me via email at faranabbas@hotmail.com.
This project analyzes how fiscal policy and international trade have influenced GDP growth across SAARC countries from 2000 to 2024. It combines data visualization, policy analysis, and economic indicators using data sourced from the World Bank. The full project repository is available here.
This project was developed as part of Kane’s Data Science Bootcamp, which emphasizes reproducible research and open-source tools using R and Quarto.

title: Fiscal Balance, Trade Openness, and GDP in SAARC Countries (2000–2024)
text:
Summary This project investigates the trends in fiscal balance, trade openness, and GDP among SAARC countries from 2000 to 2024 using World Bank WDI data. The analysis focuses on Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.
Key Insights:

Trade openness has expanded in several countries—most notably India and Bangladesh—indicating stronger economic integration.
Fiscal revenue patterns differ, reflecting varying government capacities and policies.
GDP growth is uneven, with countries like India showing sustained growth, while others such as Afghanistan and Nepal exhibit volatility.

These observations serve as a foundation for deeper policy discussion, especially around how fiscal strategies and international trade engagement affect economic performance in developing regions.
